summary: Normalizes the quaternion a2 (x,y,z,w) to unit length and writes the result into a1 (in-place safe). Computes the squared norm v8 = a2[0]^2 + a2[1]^2 + a2[2]^2 + a2[3]^2; if FloatRangeCheck(v8, 1.0) passes the input is already unit length and is copied (or returned without copy when a1 == a2). Otherwise, when v8 exceeds 1.1754944e-38 the quaternion is scaled by 1/sqrt(v8); when v8 is at or below that threshold all four output components are zeroed. Every path writes all four output components, so an external poke to the output does not persist.

local_names.a2: input quaternion buffer (x,y,z,w), may alias a1
local_names.v8: squared norm of the input quaternion
local_names.v5: reciprocal square root 1/sqrt(v8) used as the scaling factor
local_names.v7: scratch normalized-component buffer for the aliasing case

operations.description: Compute the squared norm v8 = a2[0]*a2[0] + a2[1]*a2[1] + a2[2]*a2[2] + a2[3]*a2[3].
Call FloatRangeCheck(v8, 1.0) to test whether the squared norm is within the symmetric epsilon band of 1.0, i.e. whether the quaternion is already unit length.
When FloatRangeCheck returns true the quaternion is already normalized: copy a2 into a1, or return immediately when a1 == a2 (in-place call).
When v8 > 1.1754944e-38 compute the scaling factor v5 = 1.0 / sqrt(v8) and build the normalized vector in a scratch buffer; when v8 <= 1.1754944e-38 skip normalization.

Write the four output components: on the normalization path each output equals v5 times the corresponding input component; on the too-small path all four outputs are zeroed; on the already-unit path they are a straight copy of the input.
Return the output buffer pointer a1.

clean_pseudocode: float tmp[4] = { inv*a2[0], inv*a2[1], inv*a2[2], inv*a2[3] };
